title: Lie groups, Part II: parabolic subgroups, Langlands decompositions and the Bruhat decomposition of real reductive groups
summary: Continue LieGroups Layer 9 retaining its full finite central matrix-cover Cartan datum and adding a compatible invariant form. Prove conjugacy of underlying involutions and Iwasawa choices with equal split centres, without identifying forms or auxiliary models. Extend minimal-parabolic and Langlands theory to compatible nonalgebraic finite covers and disconnected groups; prove Bruhat and Tits theory, standard parabolic classification and Langlands decompositions, the component-fixed split-centre character decomposition, and the dynamical description. Adapt the supplied polar theorem to the intrinsic matrix tangent algebra. Consume AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups 2.3a's minimal algebraic comparison and extend it to all chamber faces.

layers.title: Reductive Cartan data and their conjugacy

targets.name: ReductiveCartanDatum
targets.statement: A reductive Cartan datum is a full LieGroups CartanInvolution I G, including global_model : FiniteCartanMatrixModel G θ, together with a symmetric nondegenerate bilinear form B on 𝔤, invariant under Ad(G) and dθ, with 𝔨 ⊥ 𝔭, negative on 𝔨 and positive on 𝔭. Retain the finite central covering onto a closed transpose-stable finite-component matrix subgroup, compatibility with transpose-inverse and pointwise fixation of the compact preimage. Consume the base polar diffeomorphism; do not add it as a field or a new theorem.
hypotheses: G is a real finite-dimensional C^infinity Lie group (LieGroup I ∞ G, FiniteDimensional ℝ E, T2Space G, BoundarylessManifold I G), 𝔤 = LeftInvariantDerivation I G

locator.where: Ch. VII §2 (reductive Lie groups and their axioms)

layers.title: Restricted roots, positive systems and the two Weyl groups

targets.name: RootSystem.positiveSystem
targets.statement: For a finite crystallographic root system Φ (possibly non-reduced) in V: a positive system is Φ⁺ = {β : β(v) > 0} for v regular; its simple roots are the elements of Φ⁺ that are not sums of two elements of Φ⁺; Φ_ind = {β : β/2 ∉ Φ}. hypotheses: Φ a finite crystallographic root system in a real vector space, possibly non-reduced

targets.statement: For a reductive Cartan group L define ⁰L as the joint kernel of all continuous χ:L→ℝ_{>0}, V=𝔷(𝔩)∩𝔭_L, F=V^{Ad(L)}, V₀=F^⊥∩V for Bθ, and A_L=lieExp V. The component action on V is finite and orthogonal; its average is pr_F. The homomorphism h:L→F sends k exp X to the projection of X's split-central part, and positive characters are exactly exp∘ℓ∘h, ℓ∈F*. Thus ⁰L is closed normal, Lie(⁰L)=[𝔩,𝔩]⊕(𝔷∩𝔨_L)⊕V₀, ⁰L=K_L exp((𝔭_L∩[𝔩,𝔩])⊕V₀), the datum restricts to it, and multiplication ⁰L×exp(F)→L is a Lie-group isomorphism. When the component action on V is trivial (in particular under the component condition), F=V and V₀=0, giving ⁰L×A_L≅L. ⁰L is intrinsic; A_L and exp(F) depend on the datum.
